draft.title: Controlling infectious diseases
card: Controlling a disease means cutting its spread. Each method works in a different way, so they are often used together.
Handwashing
removes pathogens from the skin before they can be passed on by touch or reach the mouth, eyes or food.
Quarantine
keeps people who may be infected away from others, so they have less chance to pass the pathogen on.
Vaccination

prepares the immune system to fight a pathogen, so a vaccinated person is less likely to get sick or pass it on. Medical treatment helps an infected person recover. Public education campaigns teach people which actions lower the risk.
draft.remember: Each control method cuts the spread in a different way: clean, separate, prepare, treat or inform.

a.q: How does vaccination help control an infectious disease?
opts: It prepares the immune system to fight the pathogen
It removes pathogens from the skin before they spread
It keeps possibly infected people away from others
It teaches people which actions lower the risk
a.why: A vaccine prepares the immune system, so a vaccinated person is less likely to get sick or pass the disease on. Removing pathogens from the skin describes handwashing, which is a different method.
a.clue: Think about what happens inside the body before any pathogen arrives.

b.q: A student at a Geelong school has a highly infectious illness. The school asks the student to stay home until they are well. Which control method is this?
opts: Quarantine, because it keeps the student away from others
Vaccination, because it prepares other students to fight it
Handwashing, because it removes pathogens from the skin
Education, because it teaches students about the illness
b.why: Keeping a person who may be infected away from others gives the pathogen fewer chances to spread, which is quarantine. Education may have led the family to act, but the action itself is separation.
b.clue: Look at what the school actually does with the student.

a.best: It prepares the immune system to fight the pathogen

b.best: Quarantine, because it keeps the student away from others

problems.detail: The student already has the illness, so keeping them home is strictly isolation. Australian health authorities use quarantine for people who may have been exposed but are not known to be sick. The card's own definition (people who 'may be infected') fits an exposed person better than a confirmed case. Make the scenario a student who was exposed but is not yet sick, or note that separating sick people is called isolation.
